title: Compliance Conformance Spec
description: Input shape for scripts/conformance_audit.mjs — a compliance-ladder design (with its doc/schema/ui/probe surface declarations) plus adapter conformance fixtures that either back or fail to back each level with a daemon-witnessed negative probe.

order.description: Position in the ladder; 0 is the base/entry level that requires no daemon-witnessed evidence.

name.description: Human-readable level name, e.g. "Suggestible". This is exactly the field that drifted across binder docs for the same id/order (e.g. C3 "Suggestible" vs C3 "Controllable").

requiredPredicates.description: Structured predicate names this level requires be daemon-witnessed true, e.g. "tool-preflight-witnessed". Never free-text prose.

ladders.description: Canonical ladder definitions, e.g. the compliance ladder (C0-C6) and the transcript-fidelity ladder (T0-T5).

surfaces.description: Every place the ladder is independently declared: documentation prose, a JSON/type schema, the operator UI, and the compliance probe implementation itself. May be empty, but an empty array or missing kind is never treated as safe.

source.description: Optional file path or component name identifying where this surface's declaration actually lives.

adapters.description: One conformance fixture per backend under test, e.g. Codex, Claude Code, Cloudflare, Ollama/LM Studio, or a custom stdio/HTTP agent.

ladder.description: References ladders[].name this claimedLevel is measured against.

claimedLevel.description: The level id this adapter fixture claims, or is tested at.

negativeProbes.description: Hostile fixtures that try to make the adapter appear more compliant than it is. All five required kinds should appear per adapter.

present.description: True only if this hostile-probe fixture actually exists and the daemon exercised it against this adapter — not a planned/stubbed probe.

downgraded.description: True only if, having fired, the daemon correctly downgraded the adapter's effective level in response. Absent or false fails closed: an untested outcome is never assumed safe.
